title: Microcost & Latency Explorer — workshop notes and wireframe variants
body:
Summary:

This doc captures the outcomes from the Microcost & Latency Explorer workshop (09/24). Goal: produce a set of wireframe variants and a prioritized grooming list for a console view that lets customers slice token-level cost and per-token latency across routes, models, and time. The focus is tooling-first: rapid drilldowns for engineering teams to find cost hot-spots and latency regressions, and to make routing/quantization/batching choices visible.

High-level goals / success metrics:
- Surface per-route / per-model token cost and median/p95 token latency in a single unified pane.
- Allow fast drilldown from anomaly -> example requests -> full trace (100ms target for initial drilldown load).
- Provide attribution by prompt prefix, user cohort (if available), and model variant (quantized vs full).
- Exportable incident snapshots (CSV/JSON) for postmortems.
- Adoption target: used by 30% of Dedicated customers in first quarter after release; median session length < 6 minutes to identify root cause.

Key UX principles we agreed on:
1) Overview-first: customers often want to know "Is cost unusual?" and "Which model/route?" before deep diving. The top of the page should be a concise anomaly summary and timepicker.
2) Guided drilldown: provide a breadcrumb-style exploration path: Overview -> Route -> Model Version -> Example Requests -> Full Trace.
3) Lightweight sampling: full per-token traces are large. Surface sampled aggregates by default with a clear sample rate indicator and a button to pull raw traces for a selected time window.
4) Contextual recommendations: pair each hot-spot with concrete next steps (e.g., enable KV cache, reduce max_tokens, switch to quantized variant).

Wireframe variants (sketch descriptions):

Variant A — "Stacked lanes" (Priority prototype) - Layout: three horizontal lanes stacked vertically. Top lane: time-series sparklines (tokens, cost, median latency) with anomaly overlays and timepicker. Middle lane: breakdown by route/model (interactive table with inline sparklines, per-token-cost, p50/p95 token latency, request rate). Bottom lane: sample requests list + sample trace viewer (expandable).
- Interactions: clicking a route row filters the top lane and loads sample requests on the bottom; model-version chip toggles quantized vs baseline comparisons.
- Pros: fast overview + single-click drilldown; maps well to console real estate.
- Cons: can feel dense for many routes; needs pagination and column hiding.

Variant B — "Explorer panes" (secondary) - Layout: left column (30%) = filters & metadata (teams, project tags, route list); center (50%) = main chart area (cost & latency stacked chart with dual y-axis); right (20%) = contextual recommendations and quick actions (toggle batching, cache, pin model).
- Interactions: drag-to-zoom on chart to narrow time window; quick-action buttons apply simulated cost delta (estimates) before commit.
- Pros: clearer filter affordance; good for operational playbooks.
- Cons: more clicks to reach sample requests; less emphasis on example-level debugging.

Variant C — "Incident-first" (for on-call flows) - Layout: single column feed of anomalies/top hot-spots. Each card expands to show the cost/latency mini-visualization and a button to "Open investigation" which opens Variant A style drilldown modal.
- Pros: great for SRE/on-call; aligns with adoptable alert workflows.
- Cons: not ideal for exploratory cost optimization sessions.

Data model & sampling notes:
- Source dimensions: timestamp, route_id, model_id, model_variant, org_id, user_cohort (nullable), tokens_in, tokens_out, per_token_latencies (array or summarized quantiles), cost_per_token (USD).
- Default aggregation window: 1h for >7d range, 5m for last 6h. UI exposes controls.
- Sampling: default 1% raw trace sampling for high-volume routes; allow on-demand increase to 100% for selected short windows. Show sampling rate badge.
- Approx cost computation: use token accounting consistent with billing (including rounding/reservation rules). Provide toggle to view raw token count vs billing tokens.

Metrics definitions (to surface, exact labels for the UI):
- avg_token_cost_usd (mean cost per token in USD)
- total_tokens (sum tokens_in + tokens_out)
- req_rate_rps (requests per second)
- median_token_latency_ms (p50 per-token)
- p95_token_latency_ms
- kv_cache_hit_rate (when applicable)
- model_variant_delta_pct (cost or latency percent difference vs baseline model)

Backlog / groom priorities (ranked):
1) Core analytics + stacked-lanes wireframe prototype (Variant A) — include sample request list and model-version comparison chips. (owner: Priya)
2) API and indexing: small schema change to keep per-token latency histograms (ENG ticket ENG-10234) — blocked by infra storage config. (owner: Samir)
3) Sampling controls + sample-rate badge + explanatory tooltip (owner: Diego)
4) Simulated cost estimator UI (estimates of cost change for toggling batching/quantization) — UX research needed. (owner: Maya)
5) Incident card feed + alert attachments (Variant C) — integrate with existing alerting (PagerDuty/Slack). (owner: Leah)
6) Export snapshot (CSV/JSON) + attachable to support tickets. (owner: Priya)
7) Onboarding/inline help copy (microcopy + tooltips) — coordinate with docs. (owner: Product Docs)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Data retention & query cost: what historical resolution can infra support for per-token histograms beyond 30 days? (ENG infra)
- Sample rate defaults: should sampling be org-configurable or per-route? Preference in workshop: per-org default, per-route override.
- Privacy: how to mask PII in example prompts when surfacing examples? Product legal to propose masking defaults.
- Export format: include raw token latencies arrays or only summary stats? Proposed: include raw arrays only when requester has export permission (audit logs).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI implements Variant A with: top time-series, middle interactive table of routes/models, bottom sample requests list and a trace viewer.
- Drilldown latency: initial route->samples load <= 1000ms for median expected dataset (dedicated small org).
- Sampling indicator visible and accurate for all sampled views.
- Cost numbers match billing within +/- 2% for the displayed time window.
- Exports produce CSV with the same aggregated rows shown in the UI.

Accessibility & performance notes:
- Charts should be keyboard-navigable and have high contrast options.
- Heavy client-side work (trace viewer) should lazy-load and fall back to server-rendered snapshot for low-spec browsers.

Next steps & owners (short-term 2-week plan):
- Prototype Variant A in Figma and demo to eng (Priya, 1 week).
- Spike on per-token histograms indexing and cost of storing last-90d (Samir, 1 week).
- Create ENG-10234 with concrete schema and infra cost estimate (Samir).
- Build a small data shim to return sampled example traces for the prototype (Diego).

Meeting note (09/24 workshop):
Attendees: Maya, Priya, Samir, Diego, Leah.
Decisions: Prototype Variant A first; sampling badge mandatory; allow per-org sample default.
Action items assigned in backlog above.

Open artifacts to attach for next sync:
- Figma: initial frames (TBD link in linked_artifacts once created)
- Spike doc (ENG-10234)

If you want to prioritize a different variant for the prototype (e.g., Incident-first), flag by EOD Monday and note the rationale (on-call adoption vs exploratory cost optimization).

Revision history:
- 2024-09-30 initial workshop notes (Maya)
- 2024-10-02 added backlog priorities and owners (Priya)
- 2024-10-14 updated acceptance criteria and linked artifacts (Maya)
